@SearchOrchestratorRegistry.register('serial')
class SearchOrchestrator: 
 224@SearchOrchestratorRegistry.register("serial")
 225class SearchOrchestrator:
 226    """
 227    Main orchestrator for DFTScape search algorithms.
 228
 229    This class serves as the central coordinator for high-dimensional search operations
 230    in DFTScape, managing the complete lifecycle of molecular landscape exploration.
 231    It orchestrates the interaction between search strategies, job execution, graph
 232    management, and monitoring systems to provide robust and efficient search capabilities.
 233
 234    Key Features:
 235    - **Dual Search Modes**: Separate upward and downward search algorithms
 236    - **Strategy Pattern**: Pluggable search strategies for different algorithms
 237    - **Job Lifecycle Management**: Complete job creation, execution, and tracking
 238    - **Graph Coordination**: Integration with SearchableCriticalPointGraph
 239    - **State Management**: Comprehensive node processing state tracking
 240    - **Progress Monitoring**: Real-time monitoring with detailed statistics
 241    - **Checkpoint Support**: Full state persistence and restoration
 242    - **Callback Integration**: Extensible callback system for custom logic
 243    - **Error Resilience**: Robust error handling and recovery mechanisms
 244
 245    The orchestrator coordinates these core components:
 246    - **Search Strategies**: FirstNontrivialUpwardSearchStrategy and ExhaustiveDownwardSearchStrategy
 247    - **Job Management**: JobQueues for scheduling, JobTracker for lifecycle tracking
 248    - **Execution**: JobExecutor for running HiSD calculations
 249    - **State Tracking**: NodeStateManager for processing coordination
 250    - **Monitoring**: SearchMonitor for performance analytics
 251    - **Persistence**: CheckpointRegistry for state management
 252
 253    Attributes:
 254        graph (SearchableCriticalPointGraph): The searchable graph containing critical points
 255        job_queues (JobQueues): Manager for pending job queues
 256        d_max (Optional[int]): Maximum search order for upward search (None = unlimited)
 257        job_tracker (JobTracker): Tracker for job lifecycle and dependencies
 258        node_states (NodeStateManager): Manager for node processing states
 259        executor (JobExecutor): Executor for running HiSD jobs
 260        perturbation_magnitude (float): Default perturbation magnitude for job spawning
 261        upward_strategy (FirstNontrivialUpwardSearchStrategy): Strategy for upward search
 262        downward_strategy (ExhaustiveDownwardSearchStrategy): Strategy for downward search
 263        callbacks (Optional[List[OrchestratorCallback]]): Callbacks for state change events
 264        monitor (SearchMonitor): Monitor for search performance and statistics
 265
 266    Usage Examples:
 267        >>> from dftscape.core.search_orchestrator import SearchOrchestrator
 268        >>> from dftscape.core.graph import SearchableCriticalPointGraph
 269        >>> from dftscape.core.job_queues import JobQueues
 270        >>>
 271        >>> # Initialize components
 272        >>> graph = SearchableCriticalPointGraph(threshold=0.1)
 273        >>> job_queues = JobQueues()
 274        >>> hisd_runner = HiSDRunner(...)
 275        >>>
 276        >>> # Create orchestrator with custom parameters
 277        >>> orchestrator = SearchOrchestrator(
 278        ...     graph=graph,
 279        ...     job_queues=job_queues,
 280        ...     hisd_runner=hisd_runner,
 281        ...     d_max=3,  # Limit search depth
 282        ...     perturbation_magnitude=0.05  # Smaller perturbations
 283        ... )
 284        >>>
 285        >>> # Run upward search
 286        >>> orchestrator.run_upward_search()
 287        >>>
 288        >>> # Check progress
 289        >>> if orchestrator.is_upward_search_complete():
 290        ...     print("Upward search finished!")
 291        ...     orchestrator.run_downward_search()
 292        >>>
 293        >>> # Run complete search
 294        >>> orchestrator.run_full_search()
 295        >>>
 296        >>> # Get comprehensive report
 297        >>> report = orchestrator.report()
 298        >>> print(report)
 299
 300    Advanced Configuration:
 301        >>> # With custom callbacks
 302        >>> from dftscape.core.callbacks import OrchestratorCallback
 303        >>>
 304        >>> class ProgressCallback(OrchestratorCallback):
 305        ...     def on_state_change(self, orchestrator):
 306        ...         stats = orchestrator.monitor.get_search_statistics("upward")
 307        ...         if stats:
 308        ...             print(f"Progress: {stats.completed_jobs}/{stats.total_jobs} jobs")
 309        >>>
 310        >>> orchestrator = SearchOrchestrator(
 311        ...     graph=graph,
 312        ...     job_queues=job_queues,
 313        ...     hisd_runner=hisd_runner,
 314        ...     callbacks=[ProgressCallback()]
 315        ... )
 316
 317    Integration Notes:
 318        - The orchestrator automatically manages job dependencies and execution order
 319        - Node states are tracked separately for upward and downward searches
 320        - The d_max parameter prevents exponential growth in upward search
 321        - Callbacks are triggered after significant events (state changes, graph changes)
 322        - The monitor provides detailed statistics and progress tracking
 323        - Checkpoint functionality enables resuming long-running searches
 324
 325    Performance Considerations:
 326        - Large graphs benefit from periodic checkpointing
 327        - The perturbation_magnitude affects search thoroughness vs. efficiency
 328        - Job batching reduces overhead in high-throughput scenarios
 329        - Parallel execution (when available) significantly improves performance
 330        - Memory usage scales with graph size and job queue depth
 331    """
 332
 333    def __init__(
 334        self,
 335        graph: SearchableCriticalPointGraph,
 336        job_queues: JobQueues,
 337        hisd_runner: HiSDRunner,
 338        d_max: Optional[int] = None,
 339        perturbation_magnitude: float = 0.1,
 340        callbacks: Optional[List[OrchestratorCallback]] = None,
 341    ):
 342        """
 343        Initialize the search orchestrator.
 344
 345        Creates a fully configured orchestrator instance with all necessary components
 346        for running high-dimensional search algorithms. The orchestrator sets up
 347        search strategies, job management systems, and monitoring infrastructure.
 348
 349        Args:
 350            graph: The searchable graph to work with. This contains the critical
 351                  points and provides methods for adding nodes, edges, and distance
 352                  calculations. The graph serves as the central data structure
 353                  for the search process.
 354            job_queues: The job queues manager for handling pending jobs. This
 355                       component manages job scheduling, prioritization, and
 356                       execution order for both upward and downward searches.
 357            hisd_runner: The HiSD runner for executing quantum chemistry calculations.
 358                        This interface abstracts the computational backend and
 359                        provides methods for running HiSD calculations and
 360                        extracting critical points.
 361            d_max: Maximum search order (Morse index) for upward search. When
 362                  specified, nodes with index >= d_max will not spawn new jobs,
 363                  preventing exponential growth. If None, no limit is applied.
 364                  Typical values: 2-5 depending on system size and computational
 365                  resources.
 366            perturbation_magnitude: Default magnitude for coordinate perturbations
 367                                   when spawning search jobs. This affects the
 368                                   exploration radius around each critical point.
 369                                   Smaller values (0.01-0.05) provide more precise
 370                                   but slower searches; larger values (0.1-0.2)
 371                                   enable broader exploration but may miss details.
 372            callbacks: Optional list of callback instances to be notified after
 373                      job batch execution. Callbacks receive the orchestrator
 374                      instance and can implement custom logic for monitoring,
 375                      logging, or integration with external systems.
 376
 377        Raises:
 378            TypeError: If required parameters are missing or have incorrect types
 379            ValueError: If parameter values are invalid (e.g., negative d_max)
 380
 381        Example:
 382            >>> from dftscape.core.search_orchestrator import SearchOrchestrator
 383            >>> from dftscape.core.graph import SearchableCriticalPointGraph
 384            >>> from dftscape.core.job_queues import JobQueues
 385            >>>
 386            >>> # Basic initialization
 387            >>> orchestrator = SearchOrchestrator(
 388            ...     graph=SearchableCriticalPointGraph(threshold=0.1),
 389            ...     job_queues=JobQueues(),
 390            ...     hisd_runner=my_hisd_runner
 391            ... )
 392            >>>
 393            >>> # Advanced configuration
 394            >>> orchestrator = SearchOrchestrator(
 395            ...     graph=my_graph,
 396            ...     job_queues=my_queues,
 397            ...     hisd_runner=my_hisd_runner,
 398            ...     d_max=3,  # Limit to Morse index 3
 399            ...     perturbation_magnitude=0.05,  # Precise search
 400            ...     callbacks=[my_progress_callback]
 401            ... )
 402
 403        Notes:
 404            - The orchestrator starts with serial execution (max_concurrent=1)
 405            - Search strategies are initialized with the provided perturbation_magnitude
 406            - The monitor is automatically enabled for tracking search performance
 407            - Callbacks are called after significant events like state changes
 408            - The d_max parameter only affects upward search; downward search is unlimited
 409        """
 410        if not isinstance(graph, SearchableCriticalPointGraph):
 411            raise TypeError("graph must be a SearchableCriticalPointGraph instance")
 412        if not isinstance(job_queues, JobQueues):
 413            raise TypeError("job_queues must be a JobQueues instance")
 414        if d_max is not None and d_max < 0:
 415            raise ValueError("d_max must be non-negative or None")
 416        if perturbation_magnitude <= 0:
 417            raise ValueError("perturbation_magnitude must be positive")
 418
 419        self.graph = graph
 420        self.job_queues = job_queues
 421        self.d_max = d_max
 422        self.job_tracker = JobTracker()
 423        self.node_states = NodeStateManager(graph)
 424        self.executor = JobExecutor(hisd_runner, max_concurrent=1)  # Start with serial
 425
 426        # Search parameters
 427        self.perturbation_magnitude = perturbation_magnitude
 428
 429        # Use composition with strategies (configured with default perturbation magnitude)
 430        self.upward_strategy = FirstNontrivialUpwardSearchStrategy(
 431            perturbation_magnitude=self.perturbation_magnitude
 432        )
 433        self.downward_strategy = ExhaustiveDownwardSearchStrategy(
 434            perturbation_magnitude=self.perturbation_magnitude
 435        )
 436
 437        # Callbacks for job batch completion
 438        self.callbacks = callbacks
 439
 440        # Statistics and monitoring
 441        self.monitor: SearchMonitor = SearchMonitor()
 442
 443    def run_upward_search(self) -> None:
 444        """
 445        Run the upward search algorithm using the configured upward strategy.
 446
 447        This method executes the upward search phase, which explores the molecular
 448        landscape by finding critical points of increasing Morse index. The search
 449        uses the FirstNontrivialUpwardSearchStrategy with the perturbation magnitude
 450        specified during initialization.
 451
 452        The upward search process:
 453        1. Starts from existing critical points in the graph
 454        2. Spawns jobs to find higher-index critical points via perturbations
 455        3. Adds newly discovered points to the graph
 456        4. Continues until no new jobs can be spawned or d_max is reached
 457        5. Respects the d_max limit to prevent exponential growth
 458
 459        The search completes when:
 460        - All nodes have been processed for upward search
 461        - The job queue is empty
 462        - No new jobs can be generated (due to d_max or strategy constraints)
 463
 464        Example:
 465            >>> orchestrator = SearchOrchestrator(...)
 466            >>> orchestrator.run_upward_search()
 467            >>> if orchestrator.is_upward_search_complete():
 468            ...     print("Upward search completed successfully")
 469
 470        Notes:
 471            - This method blocks until the search completes
 472            - Progress can be monitored via the monitor attribute
 473            - The search respects the d_max parameter set during initialization
 474            - Callbacks are triggered after each job batch completion
 475            - Statistics are automatically collected and available via get_statistics()
 476        """
 477        self.run_search(self.upward_strategy, "upward")
 478
 479    def run_search(self, strategy: "SearchStrategy", procedure: str) -> None:
 480        """
 481        Run a search using the given strategy and procedure type.
 482
 483        This is the core search execution method that implements the main search
 484        algorithm loop. It coordinates job spawning, execution, and result processing
 485        according to the specified search strategy and procedure type.
 486
 487        The search algorithm follows this pattern:
 488        1. Initialize search state and monitoring
 489        2. While search is not finished:
 490           a. Get unprocessed nodes for this procedure
 491           b. For each node, spawn jobs using the strategy
 492           c. Add spawned jobs to the execution queue
 493           d. Execute pending jobs and process results
 494           e. Log progress and trigger callbacks
 495        3. Finalize search and generate completion statistics
 496
 497        Args:
 498            strategy: The search strategy to use for job spawning. This determines
 499                     how jobs are generated from each critical point and what
 500                     perturbations are applied.
 501            procedure: The search procedure type ("upward" or "downward").
 502                      This affects node state tracking and job spawning logic.
 503
 504        Raises:
 505            ValueError: If procedure is not "upward" or "downward"
 506            RuntimeError: If strategy execution fails critically
 507
 508        Example:
 509            >>> # Run upward search
 510            >>> orchestrator.run_search(orchestrator.upward_strategy, "upward")
 511            >>>
 512            >>> # Run downward search
 513            >>> orchestrator.run_search(orchestrator.downward_strategy, "downward")
 514
 515        Notes:
 516            - This method blocks until the search completes
 517            - Job execution is batched for efficiency
 518            - Failed jobs are logged but don't stop the search
 519            - Progress is logged at regular intervals
 520            - The monitor tracks detailed statistics throughout
 521        """
 522        self._initialize_search(procedure)
 523
 524        while not self._is_search_finished(procedure):
 525            # For each unprocessed node, ask the strategy which RunConditions to spawn
 526            unprocessed_nodes = self.node_states.get_unprocessed_nodes(procedure)
 527            logger.debug(f"Found {len(unprocessed_nodes)} unprocessed nodes")
 528
 529            for node_id in unprocessed_nodes:
 530                if node_id not in self.graph._graph.nodes:
 531                    logger.warning(f"Node {node_id} not found in graph")
 532                    self.node_states.mark_processed(node_id, procedure)
 533                    continue
 534
 535                # Use helper method to spawn jobs (handles all strategy delegation and job ID creation)
 536                jobs = self._spawn_jobs_from_node(node_id, procedure)
 537
 538                # If no jobs were spawned for this node, mark it as processed immediately
 539                if not jobs:
 540                    self.node_states.mark_processed(node_id, procedure)
 541                    logger.debug(
 542                        f"Node {node_id} marked processed immediately (no jobs spawned)"
 543                    )
 544                else:
 545                    # Add to queues and tracker, then mark node as processing
 546                    self.job_queues.add_jobs(procedure, jobs)
 547                    job_ids = [job_id for job_id, _ in jobs]
 548                    self.job_tracker.add_jobs_for_node(node_id, job_ids)
 549                    self.node_states.mark_processing(node_id, procedure)
 550                    logger.debug(
 551                        f"Node {node_id} marked as processing with {len(jobs)} jobs spawned"
 552                    )
 553
 554            # Execute pending jobs and log progress
 555            self._execute_pending_jobs(procedure)
 556            self._log_progress(procedure)
 557
 558        self._finalize_search(procedure)
 559
 560    def run_downward_search(self) -> None:
 561        """
 562        Run the downward search algorithm using the configured downward strategy.
 563
 564        This method executes the downward search phase, which explores connections
 565        between critical points by finding transition paths and lower-index saddles.
 566        The search uses the ExhaustiveDownwardSearchStrategy with the perturbation
 567        magnitude specified during initialization.
 568
 569        The downward search process:
 570        1. Requires upward search to be complete first
 571        2. Starts from all critical points in the graph
 572        3. Spawns jobs to find transition paths to lower-index points
 573        4. Adds transition edges between connected critical points
 574        5. Continues until all possible transitions are explored
 575
 576        Prerequisites:
 577        - Upward search must be completed first
 578        - Graph must contain critical points from upward search
 579        - No d_max limit (downward search explores all connections)
 580
 581        Raises:
 582            RuntimeError: If upward search is not complete
 583
 584        Example:
 585            >>> orchestrator = SearchOrchestrator(...)
 586            >>> orchestrator.run_upward_search()  # Must complete first
 587            >>> orchestrator.run_downward_search()
 588            >>> if orchestrator.is_downward_search_complete():
 589            ...     print("Full landscape exploration completed")
 590
 591        Notes:
 592            - This method blocks until the search completes
 593            - Downward search adds edges to the graph representing transitions
 594            - The search explores all possible connections between critical points
 595            - Progress monitoring is available via the monitor attribute
 596            - Callbacks are triggered for graph changes and state changes
 597        """
 598        # Step 1: Synchronization check
 599        if not self.is_upward_search_complete():
 600            raise RuntimeError(
 601                "Cannot start downward search: upward search is not complete"
 602            )
 603
 604        # Step 2: preserve any loaded node state (no re-initialization)
 605        self.run_search(self.downward_strategy, "downward")
 606
 607    def run_full_search(self) -> None:
 608        """
 609        Run the complete search algorithm: upward search followed by downward search.
 610
 611        This method provides a convenient way to execute the full landscape exploration
 612        process, automatically sequencing the upward and downward search phases. It
 613        uses the strategies' configured perturbation magnitudes and respects all
 614        initialization parameters.
 615
 616        The full search process:
 617        1. Execute upward search to find all critical points
 618        2. Verify upward search completion
 619        3. Execute downward search to find all transition connections
 620        4. Generate final completion statistics
 621
 622        This is equivalent to calling:
 623        >>> orchestrator.run_upward_search()
 624        >>> if orchestrator.is_upward_search_complete():
 625        ...     orchestrator.run_downward_search()
 626
 627        Example:
 628            >>> orchestrator = SearchOrchestrator(...)
 629            >>> orchestrator.run_full_search()
 630            >>> print("Complete landscape exploration finished")
 631            >>> report = orchestrator.report()
 632            >>> print(report)
 633
 634        Notes:
 635            - This method blocks until both search phases complete
 636            - If upward search fails to complete, downward search is skipped
 637            - Progress monitoring covers both search phases
 638            - Final statistics include metrics from both upward and downward searches
 639            - The graph will contain all critical points and their connections
 640        """
 641        logger.debug("Starting full search (upward + downward)")
 642
 643        # Phase 1: Upward search
 644        self.run_upward_search()
 645
 646        # Phase 2: Downward search (only if upward is complete)
 647        if self.is_upward_search_complete():
 648            self.run_downward_search()
 649        else:
 650            logger.error("Cannot proceed to downward search: upward search incomplete")
 651
 652        logger.debug("Full search completed")
 653
 654    def _initialize_search(self, procedure: str) -> None:
 655        """
 656        Initialize the state for a search procedure.
 657
 658        This method sets up the necessary state for starting a new search procedure,
 659        including logging the start event and initializing monitoring. It ensures
 660        that all components are properly configured before the search begins.
 661
 662        Args:
 663            procedure: The search procedure type ("upward" or "downward") being initialized.
 664
 665        Notes:
 666            - Logs the search start with relevant parameters
 667            - Initializes monitoring for the procedure
 668            - Validates that the procedure type is supported
 669            - Called automatically by run_search() method
 670        """
 671        logger.debug(f"Starting {procedure} search")
 672        if procedure == "upward" and self.d_max is not None:
 673            logger.debug(f"Maximum search order (d_max): {self.d_max}")
 674
 675        # Start monitoring the search
 676        self.monitor.start_search(procedure)
 677
 678    def _is_search_finished(self, procedure: str) -> bool:
 679        """
 680        Check if a search procedure has completed.
 681
 682        Determines whether a search procedure has finished by checking both the
 683        job queue status and node processing state. A search is considered complete
 684        when there are no pending jobs, no unprocessed nodes remaining, and no
 685        nodes currently being processed.
 686
 687        Args:
 688            procedure: The search procedure type ("upward" or "downward") to check.
 689
 690        Returns:
 691            True if the search is complete, False otherwise.
 692
 693        Notes:
 694            - Checks job queue emptiness, unprocessed nodes, and processing nodes
 695            - Used by the main search loop to determine when to exit
 696            - Critical for preventing infinite loops in search execution
 697        """
 698        queue_empty = self.job_queues.is_queue_empty(procedure)
 699        has_unprocessed = self.node_states.has_unprocessed_nodes(procedure)
 700        processing_count = len(self.node_states.get_processing_nodes(procedure))
 701
 702        logger.debug(
 703            f"DEBUG _is_search_finished({procedure}): queue_empty={queue_empty}, has_unprocessed={has_unprocessed}, processing_count={processing_count}"
 704        )
 705
 706        finished = queue_empty and not has_unprocessed and processing_count == 0
 707        if not finished:
 708            logger.debug(
 709                f"DEBUG: Search not finished - queue_empty={queue_empty}, unprocessed={has_unprocessed}, processing={processing_count}"
 710            )
 711
 712        return finished
 713        # return (
 714        #     self.job_queues.is_queue_empty(procedure)
 715        #     and not self.node_states.has_unprocessed_nodes(procedure)
 716        #     and len(self.node_states.get_processing_nodes(procedure)) == 0
 717        # )
 718
 719    def _spawn_jobs_for_unprocessed_nodes(self, procedure: str) -> None:
 720        """Spawn jobs for unprocessed nodes."""
 721        unprocessed_nodes = self.node_states.get_unprocessed_nodes(procedure)
 722        logger.debug(f"Found {len(unprocessed_nodes)} unprocessed nodes")
 723
 724        for node_id in unprocessed_nodes:
 725            jobs = self._spawn_jobs_from_node(node_id, procedure)
 726
 727            if jobs:
 728                self.job_queues.add_jobs(procedure, jobs)
 729                # Mark node as processing when jobs are spawned
 730                self.node_states.mark_processing(node_id, procedure)
 731                logger.debug(
 732                    f"Spawned {len(jobs)} jobs for node {node_id} and marked as processing"
 733                )
 734                # Trigger callbacks after spawning jobs to allow checkpointing
 735                if self.callbacks is not None:
 736                    # Callbacks triggered when job queue status changes (jobs added)
 737                    for callback in self.callbacks:
 738                        callback.on_state_change(self)
 739            else:
 740                # No jobs spawned - mark as processed immediately
 741                self.node_states.mark_processed(node_id, procedure)
 742                logger.debug(f"Node {node_id} marked as processed (no jobs to spawn)")
 743
 744    def _execute_pending_jobs(self, procedure: str) -> None:
 745        """
 746        Execute pending jobs one-by-one for a procedure.
 747
 748        This method processes jobs in the queue individually, executing them
 749        through the job executor and handling their results. Jobs are removed
 750        from the queue after execution since the algorithm is deterministic -
 751        whether successful or failed, retrying won't produce different results.
 752
 753        Args:
 754            procedure: The search procedure type ("upward" or "downward")
 755                      whose pending jobs should be executed.
 756
 757        Notes:
 758            - Processes jobs one-by-one to minimize loss on crashes
 759            - Executes jobs sequentially (can be extended to parallel)
 760            - Records job completion statistics in the monitor
 761            - Handles both successful and failed job results
 762            - Triggers callbacks after state changes
 763            - Updates job tracker with completion status
 764            - Failed jobs are marked complete but not re-queued
 765        """
 766        while not self.job_queues.is_queue_empty(procedure):
 767            # Peek at the next job without removing it
 768            job_info = self.job_queues.peek_job(procedure)
 769            if job_info is None:
 770                break
 771
 772            job_id, run_condition = job_info
 773
 774            # Execute the job
 775            result = self.executor.execute_job(run_condition, job_id)
 776
 777            # Record job completion in monitor
 778            self.monitor.record_job_completion(
 779                procedure=procedure,
 780                job_id=job_id,
 781                success=result.success,
 782                execution_time=result.execution_time,
 783                node_id=(
 784                    run_condition.node_id
 785                    if hasattr(run_condition, "node_id")
 786                    else job_id
 787                ),
 788            )
 789
 790            # Handle the result - wrap in try/catch to ensure job is always removed
 791            self._handle_job_result(result, procedure)
 792
 793            # Remove the job from queue since algorithm is deterministic
 794            # Whether successful or failed, retrying won't help
 795            self.job_queues.remove_job(procedure, job_id)
 796
 797            # Trigger callback after job is fully processed and removed
 798            # This ensures the job queue state is updated when the callback runs
 799            if self.callbacks is not None:
 800                for callback in self.callbacks:
 801                    callback.on_state_change(self)
 802
 803    def _handle_job_result(self, result, procedure: str) -> None:
 804        """
 805        Handle the result of a completed job execution.
 806
 807        This method processes job execution results, updating the graph, spawning
 808        new jobs, and managing node state transitions. It handles both successful
 809        and failed jobs with different logic for upward vs downward searches.
 810
 811        Args:
 812            result: The JobResult object containing execution outcome, critical
 813                   point data, and metadata.
 814            procedure: The search procedure type ("upward" or "downward") that
 815                      produced this result.
 816
 817        Notes:
 818            - For upward search: Adds new critical points to graph and spawns
 819              additional upward jobs from newly discovered points
 820            - For downward search: Finds/creates target nodes and adds transition
 821              edges between connected critical points
 822            - Handles duplicate detection automatically via graph.add()
 823            - Updates job tracker with completion status
 824            - Triggers callbacks for graph changes
 825            - Logs appropriate messages for success/failure cases
 826        """
 827        if result.success and result.critical_point is not None:
 828            # Handle successful job
 829            if procedure == "upward":
 830                # Add to graph (handles duplicates)
 831                was_added = self.graph.add(result.critical_point)
 832
 833                # Only spawn jobs from new node if it's truly unprocessed
 834                # IMPORTANT: Check node state to avoid race condition where multiple jobs
 835                # discover the same critical point and both try to spawn jobs from it
 836                if was_added:
 837                    new_node_id = result.critical_point.xyz
 838                    new_node_is_unprocessed = not self.node_states.is_processing(
 839                        new_node_id, "upward"
 840                    ) and not self.node_states.is_processed(new_node_id, "upward")
 841
 842                    if new_node_is_unprocessed:
 843                        # Spawn new jobs from the new node
 844                        new_jobs = self._spawn_jobs_from_node(new_node_id, "upward")
 845                        if new_jobs:
 846                            # Register jobs in tracker
 847                            job_ids = [job_id for job_id, _ in new_jobs]
 848                            self.job_tracker.add_jobs_for_node(new_node_id, job_ids)
 849                            # Add to queue
 850                            self.job_queues.add_jobs("upward", new_jobs)
 851                            # Mark new node as processing when jobs are spawned
 852                            self.node_states.mark_processing(new_node_id, "upward")
 853                            logger.debug(
 854                                f"Added new node {new_node_id} with {len(new_jobs)} new jobs and marked as processing"
 855                            )
 856
 857                # Mark job as complete immediately after HiSD run (for bookkeeping)
 858                parent_node_id = self._get_parent_node_id(
 859                    result.run_condition, result.job_id
 860                )
 861                logger.debug(
 862                    f"DEBUG: Marking job complete - parent_node_id='{parent_node_id}', job_id='{result.job_id}'"
 863                )
 864                self.job_tracker.mark_job_complete(
 865                    parent_node_id, result.job_id, result
 866                )
 867
 868                # Check if all jobs for this node are complete and mark node processed
 869                self._check_and_mark_node_processed(parent_node_id, procedure)
 870
 871            elif procedure == "downward":
 872                # Find or add the target node
 873                target_node_id = self._find_or_add_target_node(result.critical_point)
 874
 875                # Get the source node that spawned this job
 876                source_node_id = self._get_parent_node_id(
 877                    result.run_condition, result.job_id
 878                )
 879
 880                # Add edge between source and target (always, regardless of whether target was new)
 881                edge_changed = self._add_edge_between_nodes(
 882                    source_node_id, target_node_id, result.run_condition
 883                )
 884
 885                # Track if jobs were added to queue
 886                jobs_added = False
 887
 888                # If target node was newly added, spawn jobs from it
 889                # IMPORTANT: Check node state instead of comparing IDs to avoid race condition
 890                # where multiple jobs discover the same node simultaneously and both try to spawn jobs
 891                target_is_unprocessed = not self.node_states.is_processing(
 892                    target_node_id, "downward"
 893                ) and not self.node_states.is_processed(target_node_id, "downward")
 894
 895                if target_is_unprocessed:
 896                    # Mark the new node as upward processed since it was found through downward search
 897                    self.node_states.mark_processed(target_node_id, "upward")
 898                    logger.debug(
 899                        f"Marked new node {target_node_id} as upward processed (discovered via downward search)"
 900                    )
 901
 902                    new_jobs = self._spawn_jobs_from_node(target_node_id, "downward")
 903                    if new_jobs:
 904                        # Register jobs in tracker
 905                        job_ids = [job_id for job_id, _ in new_jobs]
 906                        self.job_tracker.add_jobs_for_node(target_node_id, job_ids)
 907                        # Add to queue
 908                        self.job_queues.add_jobs("downward", new_jobs)
 909                        # Mark new node as processing when jobs are spawned
 910                        self.node_states.mark_processing(target_node_id, "downward")
 911                        logger.debug(
 912                            f"Added new node {target_node_id} with {len(new_jobs)} new jobs and marked as processing"
 913                        )
 914                        jobs_added = True
 915
 916                # Mark job as complete immediately after HiSD run (for bookkeeping)
 917                logger.debug(
 918                    f"DEBUG: Marking job complete - source_node_id='{source_node_id}', job_id='{result.job_id}'"
 919                )
 920                self.job_tracker.mark_job_complete(
 921                    source_node_id, result.job_id, result
 922                )
 923
 924                # Check if all jobs for this node are complete and mark node processed
 925                self._check_and_mark_node_processed(source_node_id, procedure)
 926
 927            else:
 928                raise ValueError(f"Unknown procedure: {procedure}")
 929
 930        else:
 931            # Handle failed job (bookkeeping only)
 932            logger.warning(f"Job {result.job_id} failed: {result.error}")
 933            parent_node_id = self._get_parent_node_id(
 934                result.run_condition, result.job_id
 935            )
 936            logger.debug(
 937                f"DEBUG: Marking failed job complete - parent_node_id='{parent_node_id}', job_id='{result.job_id}'"
 938            )
 939            self.job_tracker.mark_job_complete(parent_node_id, result.job_id, result)
 940
 941            # Check if all jobs for this node are complete and mark node processed
 942            self._check_and_mark_node_processed(parent_node_id, procedure)
 943
 944    def _dump_node_job_state(self, node_id: str) -> str:
 945        """Return a short debug string describing job-tracker state for node_id (best-effort)."""
 946        try:
 947            pending_set = self.job_tracker.pending_jobs.get(node_id, set())
 948            completed_set = self.job_tracker.completed_jobs.get(node_id, set())
 949            # Show first few job IDs from each set
 950            pending_list = sorted(list(pending_set))[:3]
 951            completed_list = sorted(list(completed_set))[:3]
 952            return f"pending_jobs={pending_list} completed_jobs={completed_list}"
 953        except Exception as e:
 954            return f"<error reading job tracker: {e}>"
 955
 956    def _log_progress(self, procedure: str) -> None:
 957        """
 958        Log the current progress of a search procedure.
 959
 960        This method generates and logs a progress summary showing the current
 961        state of node processing and job execution for monitoring and debugging
 962        purposes. It provides real-time visibility into search advancement.
 963
 964        Args:
 965            procedure: The search procedure type ("upward" or "downward")
 966                      whose progress should be logged.
 967
 968        Notes:
 969            - Retrieves processing statistics from node state manager
 970            - Gets job execution statistics from the monitor
 971            - Logs total nodes processed vs remaining
 972            - Shows current job queue status
 973            - Includes total jobs executed count
 974            - Called periodically during search execution
 975        """
 976        stats = self.node_states.get_processing_stats(procedure)
 977        search_stats = self.monitor.search_stats.get(procedure)
 978        jobs_executed = search_stats.total_jobs if search_stats else 0
 979        queued = self.job_queues.get_queue_length(procedure)
 980
 981        # Basic progress message
 982        logger.debug(
 983            f"Progress: {stats['processed']}/{stats['total_nodes']} nodes processed, "
 984            f"{queued} jobs queued, {jobs_executed} jobs executed"
 985        )
 986
 987        # Sanity/invariant checks: processed + processing + unprocessed should equal total
 988        processed = stats.get("processed", 0)
 989        processing = stats.get("processing", 0)
 990        unprocessed = stats.get("unprocessed", 0)
 991        total_nodes = stats.get("total_nodes", 0)
 992
 993        if processed + processing + unprocessed != total_nodes:
 994            logger.warning(
 995                "Node state counts mismatch: processed(%d) + processing(%d) + unprocessed(%d) != total_nodes(%d)",
 996                processed,
 997                processing,
 998                unprocessed,
 999                total_nodes,
1000            )
1001
1002            # Dump detailed per-node diagnostics for a few nodes in each category
1003            try:
1004                processing_nodes = self.node_states.get_processing_nodes(procedure)
1005                unprocessed_nodes = set(
1006                    self.node_states.get_unprocessed_nodes(procedure)
1007                )
1008            except Exception as e:
1009                logger.exception("Failed to fetch node lists for diagnostics: %s", e)
1010                processing_nodes = []
1011                unprocessed_nodes = set()
1012
1013            # Show up to 5 processing nodes
1014            for nid in list(processing_nodes)[:5]:
1015                try:
1016                    pending = self.job_tracker.get_pending_job_count(nid)
1017                except Exception:
1018                    pending = "<err>"
1019                try:
1020                    completed = self.job_tracker.get_completed_job_count(nid)
1021                except Exception:
1022                    completed = "<err>"
1023                logger.warning(
1024                    "Processing node diagnostic: %s pending_jobs=%s completed_jobs=%s tracker_dump=%s",
1025                    nid[:120],
1026                    pending,
1027                    completed,
1028                    self._dump_node_job_state(nid),
1029                )
1030
1031            # Show up to 5 unprocessed nodes (they should have no pending/completed jobs)
1032            for nid in list(unprocessed_nodes)[:5]:
1033                try:
1034                    pending = self.job_tracker.get_pending_job_count(nid)
1035                except Exception:
1036                    pending = "<err>"
1037                try:
1038                    completed = self.job_tracker.get_completed_job_count(nid)
1039                except Exception:
1040                    completed = "<err>"
1041                logger.warning(
1042                    "Unprocessed node diagnostic: %s pending_jobs=%s completed_jobs=%s tracker_dump=%s",
1043                    nid[:120],
1044                    pending,
1045                    completed,
1046                    self._dump_node_job_state(nid),
1047                )
1048
1049        # If there are processing nodes but zero queued jobs, that's suspicious
1050        if processing > 0 and queued == 0:
1051            logger.warning(
1052                "There are %d processing nodes but job queue length is 0 for procedure '%s'",
1053                processing,
1054                procedure,
1055            )
1056            # Dump queue status and a couple of processing nodes
1057            try:
1058                logger.debug(
1059                    "JobQueues snapshot: %s", self.job_queues.get_jobs(procedure)[:5]
1060                )
1061            except Exception:
1062                logger.debug("JobQueues snapshot: <error obtaining jobs>")
1063            # Also dump per-processing-node job-tracker diagnostics to help root-cause
1064            try:
1065                processing_nodes = self.node_states.get_processing_nodes(procedure)
1066                if processing_nodes:
1067                    logger.debug(
1068                        "Processing nodes (count=%d): %s",
1069                        len(processing_nodes),
1070                        processing_nodes[:10],
1071                    )
1072                    for nid in list(processing_nodes)[:10]:
1073                        try:
1074                            pending = self.job_tracker.get_pending_job_count(nid)
1075                        except Exception:
1076                            pending = "<err>"
1077                        try:
1078                            completed = self.job_tracker.get_completed_job_count(nid)
1079                        except Exception:
1080                            completed = "<err>"
1081                        try:
1082                            tracker_dump = self._dump_node_job_state(nid)
1083                        except Exception:
1084                            tracker_dump = "<err>"
1085                        logger.warning(
1086                            "Processing-node diagnostic (proc=%s): %s pending=%s completed=%s tracker_dump=%s",
1087                            procedure,
1088                            nid[:120],
1089                            pending,
1090                            completed,
1091                            tracker_dump,
1092                        )
1093            except Exception:
1094                logger.exception("Failed to emit per-node job-tracker diagnostics")
1095
1096    def _finalize_search(self, procedure: str) -> None:
1097        """
1098        Finalize a search procedure and generate completion statistics.
1099
1100        This method performs cleanup and finalization tasks when a search
1101        procedure completes, including ending monitoring, calculating final
1102        statistics, and logging completion information.
1103
1104        Args:
1105            procedure: The search procedure type ("upward" or "downward")
1106                      that has completed.
1107
1108        Notes:
1109            - Ends monitoring for the procedure
1110            - Calculates final statistics (average job time, etc.)
1111            - Logs completion summary with timing and success metrics
1112            - Provides final status information for debugging/analysis
1113            - Called automatically when search loop exits
1114        """
1115        # End monitoring the search
1116        self.monitor.end_search(procedure)
1117
1118        # Get final statistics for logging
1119        stats = self.monitor.search_stats.get(procedure)
1120        if stats:
1121            logger.debug(
1122                f"{procedure.capitalize()} search completed in {stats.duration:.2f}s, "
1123                f"{stats.total_jobs} jobs executed, {stats.completed_jobs} successful, "
1124                f"{stats.failed_jobs} failed"
1125            )
1126
1127    def is_upward_search_complete(self) -> bool:
1128        """
1129        Check if upward search is completely finished.
1130
1131        Determines whether the upward search procedure has fully completed by
1132        verifying both job queue status and node processing state. This method
1133        is critical for coordinating the transition from upward to downward search.
1134
1135        Returns:
1136            True if upward job queue is empty AND all nodes have upward processing
1137            completed, False otherwise.
1138
1139        Notes:
1140            - Checks job queue emptiness for pending upward jobs
1141            - Verifies all nodes have been processed for upward search
1142            - Used by run_downward_search() to ensure proper sequencing
1143            - Critical for preventing premature downward search initiation
1144            - Should be checked before starting downward search
1145        """
1146        upward_queue_empty = self.job_queues.is_queue_empty("upward")
1147        all_nodes_upward_processed = not self.node_states.has_unprocessed_nodes(
1148            "upward"
1149        )
1150
1151        return upward_queue_empty and all_nodes_upward_processed
1152
1153    def is_downward_search_complete(self) -> bool:
1154        """
1155        Check if downward search is completely finished.
1156
1157        Determines whether the downward search procedure has fully completed by
1158        verifying both job queue status and node processing state. This method
1159        indicates when the complete landscape exploration is finished.
1160
1161        Returns:
1162            True if downward job queue is empty AND all nodes have downward
1163            processing completed, False otherwise.
1164
1165        Notes:
1166            - Checks job queue emptiness for pending downward jobs
1167            - Verifies all nodes have been processed for downward search
1168            - Indicates completion of full landscape exploration
1169            - Used for determining when search orchestration is finished
1170            - Can be used by external systems to monitor search progress
1171        """
1172        downward_queue_empty = self.job_queues.is_queue_empty("downward")
1173        all_nodes_downward_processed = not self.node_states.has_unprocessed_nodes(
1174            "downward"
1175        )
1176
1177        return downward_queue_empty and all_nodes_downward_processed
1178
1179    def _check_and_mark_node_processed(self, node_id: str, procedure: str) -> None:
1180        """
1181        Check if a node has all its jobs completed and mark it as processed if so.
1182
1183        This method is called immediately after each job completion to ensure
1184        nodes are marked processed without delay.
1185
1186        Args:
1187            node_id: The node ID to check
1188            procedure: The search procedure ('upward' or 'downward')
1189        """
1190        if self.job_tracker.all_jobs_complete(node_id):
1191            self.node_states.mark_processed(node_id, procedure)
1192            logger.debug(
1193                f"✓ Node {node_id} fully processed immediately after job completion"
1194            )
1195
1196    def _spawn_jobs_from_node(
1197        self, node_id: str, procedure: str
1198    ) -> List[tuple[str, RunCondition]]:
1199        """
1200        Spawn jobs from a node using the configured strategy for the procedure.
1201
1202        This method delegates job creation to the appropriate search strategy,
1203        generating RunCondition objects for exploring the landscape around a
1204        critical point. It handles strategy selection, job ID generation, and
1205        job tracking registration.
1206
1207        Args:
1208            node_id: The ID of the node from which to spawn jobs. Must exist
1209                    in the graph and contain valid critical point data.
1210            procedure: The search procedure type ("upward" or "downward")
1211                      determining which strategy to use.
1212
1213        Returns:
1214            List of (job_id, RunCondition) tuples representing the spawned jobs.
1215            Returns empty list if no jobs can be generated or if errors occur.
1216
1217        Notes:
1218            - Validates node existence in the graph before processing
1219            - Applies d_max limit for upward search to prevent exponential growth
1220            - Selects appropriate strategy based on procedure type
1221            - Generates unique job IDs with format: "{node_id}_{procedure}_{index}"
1222            - Registers jobs with job tracker for lifecycle management
1223            - Handles strategy execution errors gracefully
1224            - Returns empty list for invalid nodes or failed strategy calls
1225        """
1226        if node_id not in self.graph._graph.nodes:
1227            logger.warning(f"Node {node_id} not found in graph")
1228            return []
1229
1230        node_data = self.graph._graph.nodes[node_id]["data"]
1231
1232        # Check d_max limit for upward search (orchestrator still authoritative)
1233        if procedure == "upward" and self.d_max is not None:
1234            if node_data.index >= self.d_max:
1235                logger.debug(
1236                    f"Node {node_id} has index {node_data.index} >= d_max ({self.d_max}), skipping upward job spawning"
1237                )
1238                return []
1239
1240        # Choose strategy for this procedure
1241        if procedure == "upward":
1242            strategy = self.upward_strategy
1243        elif procedure == "downward":
1244            strategy = self.downward_strategy
1245        else:
1246            logger.error(f"Unknown procedure: {procedure}")
1247            return []
1248
1249        try:
1250            run_conditions = strategy.spawn_jobs(node_data)
1251        except Exception as e:
1252            logger.error(f"Strategy.spawn_jobs failed for node {node_id}: {e}")
1253            return []
1254
1255        if not run_conditions:
1256            return []
1257
1258        # Create job ids and return job tuples
1259        jobs: List[tuple[str, RunCondition]] = []
1260        for idx, rc in enumerate(run_conditions):
1261            job_id = f"{node_id}_{procedure}_{idx}"
1262            jobs.append((job_id, rc))
1263
1264        # NOTE: Job tracking is done by the caller (run_search) to avoid duplicate registration
1265        return jobs
1266
1267    def _get_parent_node_id(self, run_condition: RunCondition, job_id: str) -> str:
1268        """
1269        Get the parent node ID from a run condition and job ID.
1270
1271        Extracts the parent node ID from a job identifier, which follows the
1272        standard format: "{parent_node_id}_{procedure}_{job_counter}". This
1273        method is used to track job ancestry and maintain the relationship
1274        between spawned jobs and their originating nodes.
1275
1276        Args:
1277            run_condition: The RunCondition object (used as fallback for XYZ extraction)
1278            job_id: The job identifier containing the encoded parent node information
1279
1280        Returns:
1281            The parent node ID string extracted from the job_id
1282
1283        Notes:
1284            - Job IDs have format: "{parent_node_id}_{procedure}_{index}"
1285            - Uses string parsing to extract parent from "_upward_" or "_downward_" delimiters
1286            - Falls back to XYZ extraction from run_condition.state if parsing fails
1287            - Critical for maintaining job-to-node relationships in result processing
1288        """
1289        # Extract parent node ID from job_id by finding the last occurrence of '_upward_' or '_downward_'
1290        # and taking everything before that
1291        if "_upward_" in job_id:
1292            parent_node_id = job_id.rsplit("_upward_", 1)[0]
1293        elif "_downward_" in job_id:
1294            parent_node_id = job_id.rsplit("_downward_", 1)[0]
1295        else:
1296            # Fallback: use the XYZ from the run condition state
1297            logger.warning(
1298                f"Could not extract parent node ID from job_id {job_id}, falling back to XYZ computation"
1299            )
1300            parent_xyz = self.executor.hisd_runner.backend.get_xyz(run_condition.state)
1301            return parent_xyz
1302
1303        return parent_node_id
1304
1305    def _find_or_add_target_node(self, critical_point: CriticalPoint) -> str:
1306        """
1307        Find an existing node matching the critical point, or add it as a new node.
1308
1309        This method handles the addition of critical points to the search graph,
1310        implementing deduplication logic to prevent duplicate nodes within the
1311        distance threshold. When a critical point is found to be a duplicate,
1312        it returns the existing node's ID; otherwise, it adds the new point
1313        and returns its XYZ identifier.
1314
1315        Args:
1316            critical_point: The CriticalPoint object to find or add to the graph.
1317                           Must contain valid XYZ coordinates and Morse index data.
1318
1319        Returns:
1320            str: The node ID (XYZ string) of the found or added node. For new
1321                 nodes, this is the critical_point.xyz value. For duplicates,
1322                 this is the existing node's ID.
1323
1324        Notes:
1325            - Uses graph.add() method which handles distance-based deduplication
1326            - Searches all existing nodes when duplicate is detected to find match
1327            - Falls back to XYZ as node ID if duplicate search fails
1328            - Critical for maintaining graph integrity during search expansion
1329            - Distance threshold prevents numerical precision issues from creating duplicates
1330        """
1331        # Try to add the critical point (this will handle duplicates via distance)
1332        was_added = self.graph.add(critical_point)
1333
1334        if was_added:
1335            # It was a new node
1336            return critical_point.xyz
1337        else:
1338            # It was a duplicate, find the existing node
1339            # We need to search for a node with matching distance
1340            target_node_id = None
1341            for node_id, node_data in self.graph._graph.nodes(data=True):
1342                if (
1343                    self.graph.distance_function(
1344                        critical_point.xyz,
1345                        node_data["data"].xyz,
1346                        **self.graph.distance_kwargs,
1347                    )
1348                    < self.graph.threshold
1349                ):
1350                    target_node_id = node_id
1351                    break
1352
1353            if target_node_id is None:
1354                logger.error(
1355                    "Could not find existing node for duplicate critical point"
1356                )
1357                # Fallback: use the XYZ as ID anyway
1358                target_node_id = critical_point.xyz
1359
1360            return target_node_id
1361
1362    def _add_edge_between_nodes(
1363        self, source_node_id: str, target_node_id: str, run_condition: RunCondition
1364    ) -> bool:
1365        """
1366        Add a directed edge between source and target nodes with transition metadata.
1367
1368        This method creates a directed edge in the search graph representing a
1369        transition between critical points, typically from a higher-index saddle
1370        to a lower-index minimum. The edge contains metadata about the transition
1371        including the run condition that generated it and timing information.
1372
1373        Args:
1374            source_node_id: ID of the source node (typically a saddle point).
1375                           Must exist in the graph.
1376            target_node_id: ID of the target node (typically a minimum).
1377                           Must exist in the graph.
1378            run_condition: The RunCondition object that defines the transition
1379                          path from source to target, including initial state,
1380                          energy thresholds, and convergence criteria.
1381
1382        Returns:
1383            bool: True if the edge was added or its data was updated, False if
1384                  the edge already existed with identical data.
1385
1386        Notes:
1387            - Creates directed edge: source_node_id -> target_node_id
1388            - Edge metadata includes run_condition, direction, and timestamp
1389            - Direction is hardcoded as "downward" for saddle-to-minimum transitions
1390            - Logs edge creation for debugging and monitoring
1391            - Essential for maintaining connectivity in the Morse-Smale complex
1392            - Enables path reconstruction and gradient flow analysis
1393        """
1394        # Check if edge already exists and get its current data
1395        edge_exists = self.graph._graph.has_edge(source_node_id, target_node_id)
1396        old_edge_data = None
1397        if edge_exists:
1398            old_edge_data = self.graph._graph.edges[
1399                source_node_id, target_node_id
1400            ].copy()
1401
1402        # Add edge to the graph with metadata
1403        edge_data = {
1404            "run_condition": run_condition,
1405            "direction": "downward",  # This is a downward transition
1406            "created_at": time.time(),
1407        }
1408
1409        self.graph._graph.add_edge(source_node_id, target_node_id, **edge_data)
1410
1411        # Check if the edge data actually changed
1412        new_edge_data = self.graph._graph.edges[source_node_id, target_node_id]
1413        data_changed = self._compare_edge_data(old_edge_data, new_edge_data)
1414
1415        if data_changed:
1416            logger.debug(
1417                f"Added/updated downward edge from {source_node_id} to {target_node_id}"
1418            )
1419        else:
1420            logger.debug(
1421                f"Edge from {source_node_id} to {target_node_id} already exists with same data"
1422            )
1423
1424        return data_changed
1425
1426    def _compare_edge_data(self, old_data: dict, new_data: dict) -> bool:
1427        """
1428        Compare two edge data dictionaries, handling arrays properly.
1429
1430        This method safely compares edge data dictionaries that may contain
1431        numpy arrays or other objects that can't be compared with simple !=.
1432
1433        Args:
1434            old_data: The old edge data dictionary
1435            new_data: The new edge data dictionary
1436
1437        Returns:
1438            bool: True if the data is different, False if identical
1439        """
1440        if old_data is None and new_data is None:
1441            return False
1442        if old_data is None or new_data is None:
1443            return True
1444        if set(old_data.keys()) != set(new_data.keys()):
1445            return True
1446
1447        for key in old_data.keys():
1448            old_value = old_data[key]
1449            new_value = new_data[key]
1450
1451            # Handle numpy arrays
1452            if hasattr(old_value, "shape") and hasattr(new_value, "shape"):
1453                try:
1454                    import numpy as np
1455
1456                    if not np.array_equal(old_value, new_value):
1457                        return True
1458                except ImportError:
1459                    # Fallback if numpy not available
1460                    if not (old_value == new_value).all():
1461                        return True
1462            # Handle other array-like objects
1463            elif hasattr(old_value, "__len__") and hasattr(new_value, "__len__"):
1464                try:
1465                    if len(old_value) != len(new_value):
1466                        return True
1467                    # Try element-wise comparison
1468                    if not all(a == b for a, b in zip(old_value, new_value)):
1469                        return True
1470                except (TypeError, ValueError):
1471                    # If comparison fails, assume they're different
1472                    return True
1473            # Handle regular values
1474            else:
1475                try:
1476                    if old_value != new_value:
1477                        return True
1478                except ValueError:
1479                    # If comparison fails (e.g., ambiguous array truth value), assume different
1480                    return True
1481
1482        return False
1483
1484    def report(self) -> str:
1485        """
1486        Generate a comprehensive summary report of the orchestrator search status.
1487
1488        This method produces a detailed textual report by delegating to the
1489        monitor and graph components' report methods, providing a unified view
1490        of the search state.
1491
1492        Returns:
1493            str: Multi-line formatted summary report combining monitor and graph status.
1494
1495        Notes:
1496            - Delegates to monitor.report() for search statistics and node processing
1497            - Delegates to graph.report() for graph topology and critical point analysis
1498            - Adds job queue status for pending work
1499            - Used for monitoring, debugging, and progress tracking
1500        """
1501        lines = []
1502        lines.append("\n" + "=" * 80)
1503        lines.append("ORCHESTRATOR SEARCH STATUS SUMMARY")
1504        lines.append("=" * 80)
1505
1506        # Monitor status (includes search stats and node processing)
1507        lines.append("\n" + self.monitor.report(self))
1508
1509        # Graph status
1510        lines.append("\n" + self.graph.report())
1511
1512        # Job queue status (not covered by monitor or graph reports)
1513        lines.append("\n" + self.job_queues.report(self.graph))
1514
1515        lines.append("=" * 80)
1516
1517        return "\n".join(lines)

1519    @classmethod
1520    def load_checkpoint(
1521        cls,
1522        checkpoint_path: str,
1523        graph: SearchableCriticalPointGraph,
1524        hisd_runner: HiSDRunner,
1525        callbacks: Optional[List[OrchestratorCallback]] = None,
1526    ) -> "SearchOrchestrator":
1527        """
1528        Load a SearchOrchestrator instance from a checkpoint file.
1529
1530        This class method reconstructs a SearchOrchestrator from a previously
1531        saved checkpoint, restoring the search state including graph topology,
1532        job queues, and configuration parameters. It handles version compatibility
1533        and provides fallbacks for missing or corrupted data.
1534
1535        Args:
1536            checkpoint_path: Path to the JSON checkpoint file containing the
1537                           serialized orchestrator state.
1538            graph: The SearchableCriticalPointGraph instance to use. If the
1539                  checkpoint contains graph data, it will be loaded into this graph.
1540            hisd_runner: The HiSDRunner instance to use for job execution.
1541            callbacks: Optional list of OrchestratorCallback instances to be
1542                      notified of job completion events.
1543
1544        Returns:
1545            SearchOrchestrator: A fully restored orchestrator instance ready to
1546                              resume search operations from the checkpoint state.
1547
1548        Raises:
1549            FileNotFoundError: If the checkpoint file does not exist.
1550            JSONDecodeError: If the checkpoint file contains invalid JSON.
1551            Exception: For other checkpoint loading or reconstruction errors.
1552
1553        Notes:
1554            - Uses JSON checkpointer for serialization/deserialization
1555            - Restores graph topology if present in checkpoint
1556            - Reconstructs job queues with fallback for missing data
1557            - Handles both JobQueues.from_config and manual reconstruction
1558            - Preserves search configuration (d_max, perturbation_magnitude)
1559            - Critical for resuming interrupted long-running searches
1560        """
1561        # Load checkpoint data using JSON checkpointer
1562        json_checkpointer = CheckpointRegistry.create("json")
1563        checkpoint_data = json_checkpointer.load(checkpoint_path)
1564
1565        # Restore graph from checkpoint
1566        if "graph" in checkpoint_data:
1567            graph = SearchableCriticalPointGraph.from_config(checkpoint_data["graph"])
1568
1569        # Create new orchestrator instance
1570        orchestrator = cls(
1571            graph=graph,
1572            job_queues=JobQueues(),
1573            hisd_runner=hisd_runner,
1574            d_max=checkpoint_data.get("d_max"),
1575            perturbation_magnitude=checkpoint_data.get("perturbation_magnitude", 0.1),
1576            callbacks=callbacks,
1577        )
1578
1579        # Restore job queues using JobQueues.from_config if present
1580        raw_job_queues = checkpoint_data.get(
1581            "job_queues", {"upward": [], "downward": []}
1582        )
1583        try:
1584            orchestrator.job_queues = JobQueues.from_config(raw_job_queues)
1585        except Exception:
1586            # Fallback: manually reconstruct using RunCondition
1587            from .search_primitives import RunCondition
1588
1589            orchestrator.job_queues = JobQueues()
1590            for procedure, jobs in raw_job_queues.items():
1591                reconstructed = [
1592                    (job_id, RunCondition.from_config(run_condition_config))
1593                    for job_id, run_condition_config in jobs
1594                ]
1595                orchestrator.job_queues._queues[procedure] = reconstructed
1596
1597        return orchestrator

Main orchestrator for DFTScape search algorithms.

This class serves as the central coordinator for high-dimensional search operations in DFTScape, managing the complete lifecycle of molecular landscape exploration. It orchestrates the interaction between search strategies, job execution, graph management, and monitoring systems to provide robust and efficient search capabilities.

Key Features:

  • Dual Search Modes: Separate upward and downward search algorithms
  • Strategy Pattern: Pluggable search strategies for different algorithms
  • Job Lifecycle Management: Complete job creation, execution, and tracking
  • Graph Coordination: Integration with SearchableCriticalPointGraph
  • State Management: Comprehensive node processing state tracking
  • Progress Monitoring: Real-time monitoring with detailed statistics
  • Checkpoint Support: Full state persistence and restoration
  • Callback Integration: Extensible callback system for custom logic
  • Error Resilience: Robust error handling and recovery mechanisms

The orchestrator coordinates these core components:

  • Search Strategies: FirstNontrivialUpwardSearchStrategy and ExhaustiveDownwardSearchStrategy
  • Job Management: JobQueues for scheduling, JobTracker for lifecycle tracking
  • Execution: JobExecutor for running HiSD calculations
  • State Tracking: NodeStateManager for processing coordination
  • Monitoring: SearchMonitor for performance analytics
  • Persistence: CheckpointRegistry for state management
Attributes:
  • graph (SearchableCriticalPointGraph): The searchable graph containing critical points
  • job_queues (JobQueues): Manager for pending job queues
  • d_max (Optional[int]): Maximum search order for upward search (None = unlimited)
  • job_tracker (JobTracker): Tracker for job lifecycle and dependencies
  • node_states (NodeStateManager): Manager for node processing states
  • executor (JobExecutor): Executor for running HiSD jobs
  • perturbation_magnitude (float): Default perturbation magnitude for job spawning
  • upward_strategy (FirstNontrivialUpwardSearchStrategy): Strategy for upward search
  • downward_strategy (ExhaustiveDownwardSearchStrategy): Strategy for downward search
  • callbacks (Optional[List[OrchestratorCallback]]): Callbacks for state change events
  • monitor (SearchMonitor): Monitor for search performance and statistics
Usage Examples:
>>> from dftscape.core.search_orchestrator import SearchOrchestrator
>>> from dftscape.core.graph import SearchableCriticalPointGraph
>>> from dftscape.core.job_queues import JobQueues
>>>
>>> # Initialize components
>>> graph = SearchableCriticalPointGraph(threshold=0.1)
>>> job_queues = JobQueues()
>>> hisd_runner = HiSDRunner(...)
>>>
>>> # Create orchestrator with custom parameters
>>> orchestrator = SearchOrchestrator(
...     graph=graph,
...     job_queues=job_queues,
...     hisd_runner=hisd_runner,
...     d_max=3,  # Limit search depth
...     perturbation_magnitude=0.05  # Smaller perturbations
... )
>>>
>>> # Run upward search
>>> orchestrator.run_upward_search()
>>>
>>> # Check progress
>>> if orchestrator.is_upward_search_complete():
...     print("Upward search finished!")
...     orchestrator.run_downward_search()
>>>
>>> # Run complete search
>>> orchestrator.run_full_search()
>>>
>>> # Get comprehensive report
>>> report = orchestrator.report()
>>> print(report)
Advanced Configuration:
>>> # With custom callbacks
>>> from dftscape.core.callbacks import OrchestratorCallback
>>>
>>> class ProgressCallback(OrchestratorCallback):
...     def on_state_change(self, orchestrator):
...         stats = orchestrator.monitor.get_search_statistics("upward")
...         if stats:
...             print(f"Progress: {stats.completed_jobs}/{stats.total_jobs} jobs")
>>>
>>> orchestrator = SearchOrchestrator(
...     graph=graph,
...     job_queues=job_queues,
...     hisd_runner=hisd_runner,
...     callbacks=[ProgressCallback()]
... )
Integration Notes:
  • The orchestrator automatically manages job dependencies and execution order
  • Node states are tracked separately for upward and downward searches
  • The d_max parameter prevents exponential growth in upward search
  • Callbacks are triggered after significant events (state changes, graph changes)
  • The monitor provides detailed statistics and progress tracking
  • Checkpoint functionality enables resuming long-running searches
Performance Considerations:
  • Large graphs benefit from periodic checkpointing
  • The perturbation_magnitude affects search thoroughness vs. efficiency
  • Job batching reduces overhead in high-throughput scenarios
  • Parallel execution (when available) significantly improves performance
  • Memory usage scales with graph size and job queue depth
SearchOrchestrator( graph: SearchableCriticalPointGraph, job_queues: dftscape.core.job_queues.JobQueues, hisd_runner: dftscape.core.interfaces.HiSDRunner, d_max: Optional[int] = None, perturbation_magnitude: float = 0.1, callbacks: Optional[List[dftscape.core.callbacks.OrchestratorCallback]] = None) 
333    def __init__(
334        self,
335        graph: SearchableCriticalPointGraph,
336        job_queues: JobQueues,
337        hisd_runner: HiSDRunner,
338        d_max: Optional[int] = None,
339        perturbation_magnitude: float = 0.1,
340        callbacks: Optional[List[OrchestratorCallback]] = None,
341    ):
342        """
343        Initialize the search orchestrator.
344
345        Creates a fully configured orchestrator instance with all necessary components
346        for running high-dimensional search algorithms. The orchestrator sets up
347        search strategies, job management systems, and monitoring infrastructure.
348
349        Args:
350            graph: The searchable graph to work with. This contains the critical
351                  points and provides methods for adding nodes, edges, and distance
352                  calculations. The graph serves as the central data structure
353                  for the search process.
354            job_queues: The job queues manager for handling pending jobs. This
355                       component manages job scheduling, prioritization, and
356                       execution order for both upward and downward searches.
357            hisd_runner: The HiSD runner for executing quantum chemistry calculations.
358                        This interface abstracts the computational backend and
359                        provides methods for running HiSD calculations and
360                        extracting critical points.
361            d_max: Maximum search order (Morse index) for upward search. When
362                  specified, nodes with index >= d_max will not spawn new jobs,
363                  preventing exponential growth. If None, no limit is applied.
364                  Typical values: 2-5 depending on system size and computational
365                  resources.
366            perturbation_magnitude: Default magnitude for coordinate perturbations
367                                   when spawning search jobs. This affects the
368                                   exploration radius around each critical point.
369                                   Smaller values (0.01-0.05) provide more precise
370                                   but slower searches; larger values (0.1-0.2)
371                                   enable broader exploration but may miss details.
372            callbacks: Optional list of callback instances to be notified after
373                      job batch execution. Callbacks receive the orchestrator
374                      instance and can implement custom logic for monitoring,
375                      logging, or integration with external systems.
376
377        Raises:
378            TypeError: If required parameters are missing or have incorrect types
379            ValueError: If parameter values are invalid (e.g., negative d_max)
380
381        Example:
382            >>> from dftscape.core.search_orchestrator import SearchOrchestrator
383            >>> from dftscape.core.graph import SearchableCriticalPointGraph
384            >>> from dftscape.core.job_queues import JobQueues
385            >>>
386            >>> # Basic initialization
387            >>> orchestrator = SearchOrchestrator(
388            ...     graph=SearchableCriticalPointGraph(threshold=0.1),
389            ...     job_queues=JobQueues(),
390            ...     hisd_runner=my_hisd_runner
391            ... )
392            >>>
393            >>> # Advanced configuration
394            >>> orchestrator = SearchOrchestrator(
395            ...     graph=my_graph,
396            ...     job_queues=my_queues,
397            ...     hisd_runner=my_hisd_runner,
398            ...     d_max=3,  # Limit to Morse index 3
399            ...     perturbation_magnitude=0.05,  # Precise search
400            ...     callbacks=[my_progress_callback]
401            ... )
402
403        Notes:
404            - The orchestrator starts with serial execution (max_concurrent=1)
405            - Search strategies are initialized with the provided perturbation_magnitude
406            - The monitor is automatically enabled for tracking search performance
407            - Callbacks are called after significant events like state changes
408            - The d_max parameter only affects upward search; downward search is unlimited
409        """
410        if not isinstance(graph, SearchableCriticalPointGraph):
411            raise TypeError("graph must be a SearchableCriticalPointGraph instance")
412        if not isinstance(job_queues, JobQueues):
413            raise TypeError("job_queues must be a JobQueues instance")
414        if d_max is not None and d_max < 0:
415            raise ValueError("d_max must be non-negative or None")
416        if perturbation_magnitude <= 0:
417            raise ValueError("perturbation_magnitude must be positive")
418
419        self.graph = graph
420        self.job_queues = job_queues
421        self.d_max = d_max
422        self.job_tracker = JobTracker()
423        self.node_states = NodeStateManager(graph)
424        self.executor = JobExecutor(hisd_runner, max_concurrent=1)  # Start with serial
425
426        # Search parameters
427        self.perturbation_magnitude = perturbation_magnitude
428
429        # Use composition with strategies (configured with default perturbation magnitude)
430        self.upward_strategy = FirstNontrivialUpwardSearchStrategy(
431            perturbation_magnitude=self.perturbation_magnitude
432        )
433        self.downward_strategy = ExhaustiveDownwardSearchStrategy(
434            perturbation_magnitude=self.perturbation_magnitude
435        )
436
437        # Callbacks for job batch completion
438        self.callbacks = callbacks
439
440        # Statistics and monitoring
441        self.monitor: SearchMonitor = SearchMonitor()
